name: School Speed Limit When Flashing
spec: white vertical sign with black legend SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT 20 WHEN FLASHING and two yellow beacons
meaning: Obey the lower speed while the beacons flash.

snippets.back: A school speed sign that applies when flashing sets its reduced limit only while flashing; otherwise the ordinary road limit applies.
The school-zone speed on a School Speed Limit When Flashing sign applies while the lights flash; otherwise the ordinary roadway limit applies.
A school speed zone carries a reduced limit of twenty miles per hour, beginning at the SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT twenty sign and ending at the END SCHOOL ZONE sign or another posted speed sign.
A railroad crossing requires a stop when flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger or an audible train warning indicates an approaching train.
A school speed sign run by a time clock flashes yellow lights while lighting up the limit, and it is posted wherever children may be walking across the street to or from school.

Further regulations bar opposite-direction one-way entry, command merge-and-yield manners, enforce flashing-yellow school speeds with child watchfulness, warn of red-light cameras, forbid double-white-line crossings, protect green-arrow lefts while urging caution, reserve shoulders for breakdown and emergency stops, close roads to detours, and merge all traffic single-file.

Where flashing lights join the crossbuck, stop when flashing starts and wait until every train or rail vehicle has passed, the tracks are clear, and the lights stop, watching for a second train from the opposite way.

By law a driver must stop not less than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when flashing lights, lowered gates or a flagman signal a train, when a train is seen or its whistle heard, or when a stop sign stands at the crossing.

result.summary: Meaning supported by KS and LA flashing-only limit; no snippet states white vertical/black legend/two-beacon spec.
